analysis.title: Installed Building Products Inc. (IBP): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: IBP reported 3Q26 adj. EPS of $2.76, below GS's estimate and FactSet consensus of $2.83.

The miss versus GS's model came from adj. EBIT margin of 12.3%, 22bps below GS's estimate, which cost $0.05 per share. Other items cost $0.02 and taxes cost $0.03. Non-recurring items added $0.02 and revenue added $0.01.
Revenue grew 4% y/y versus GS's +3% forecast. Volumes fell 2% versus GS's -1% and -5% in 3Q25. Price/mix excluding heavy commercial was flat, in line with GS, versus +2% in 3Q25.
Heavy commercial and other segments added 3% to growth and acquisitions added 3%, versus GS's +2% estimate for acquisitions.

Adj. gross margin was 31.9%, 61bps below GS's model but inside the company's 32-34% annual target range. Rising diesel and aluminum prices and a negative shift from lower install revenue contribution pressured margin.

Single-family completions fell 12.4% y/y while IBP's single-family same branch sales fell 4.9%. Multi-family completions fell 27.3% while IBP's multi-family same branch sales rose 7.5%, which GS reads as evidence of share gains.
Commercial same branch sales grew 10% versus +12% in 3Q25.

Net debt/adj. EBITDA was 1.3x, similar to last quarter and up from 1.1x a year ago. IBP closed four acquisitions in the quarter with combined annual revenue of about $22mn, bringing YTD acquired annual sales to about $67mn. Management reaffirmed its intention to acquire $100+mn in 2026.
GS maintains a Buy rating with a $257 12-month price target based on 14.5x its Q5-Q8 EBITDA estimate. The stock closed at $235.42 on 4 Nov 2026, implying 9.2% upside.

GS's questions for the call: private versus public builder activity given higher mortgage rates, geographic changes, share gains in complementary products and multi-family, heavy and light commercial bidding and backlogs, volume versus price/mix, and inflation in materials, fuel and labor.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy after a 3Q26 adj. EPS miss of $2.76 versus $2.83 consensus. The $257 target rests on 14.5x Q5-Q8 EBITDA, and GS cites growth in complementary products, heavy commercial and multi-family share gains.

earnings_insights: IBP 3Q26 adj. EPS reported 11/5 at $2.76 versus GS estimate and FactSet consensus of $2.83.
3Q26 adj. EBIT margin reported at 12.3%, 22bps below GS estimate. Adj. gross margin reported at 31.9%, 61bps below GS model.
3Q26 revenue grew 4% y/y reported versus GS forecast of +3%. Volumes -2% versus GS -1%.
GS estimates: 9/26E EPS $2.83, 12/26E EPS $2.94, FY26E EPS $10.45, FY27E EPS $11.20, FY28E EPS $13.80. FY26E revenue $3,036.6mn and FY26E EBITDA $484.3mn.
FY25 EPS was $11.43 and 6/26 quarterly EPS was $2.91, per GS tables.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Housing completions contracted, while IBP's single-family same branch sales fell by less (-4.9%).
Multi-family completions fell sharply while IBP's same branch sales rose 7.5%.

risk_factors: Inability to identify, close and integrate acquisitions.
Greater competition if peers seek to gain share.
Loss of a key supplier could affect sales.
Higher material prices that cannot be passed through.
Inability to execute on strategic initiatives that support profitability.
Inability to attract and retain labor.
New home construction stays weaker for longer.
Rising diesel and aluminum prices and rising mortgage rates are named as margin and demand pressures.
